# Navbar Component Specification

Version: 1.2

---

## Status

**Built.** Markup is generated by
`components/site-chrome/site-chrome.js`, styles live in
`components/navbar/navbar.css`, and the scroll and toggle behaviour in
`components/navbar/navbar.js`.

The `.html` file in `components/navbar/` is a reference sheet of the CSS
classes only — editing it changes nothing on the site.

---

## Purpose

Provide clear navigation across the CEDIM website.

---

## Position

Fixed (top), `z-index:1000`

---

## Height

72 px, held by `min-height` rather than a fixed `height`.

This matters: with a fixed height the mobile menu wrapped **outside** the
box that paints the navbar background, so the links appeared over the
page content with nothing behind them. The logo and the toggle each carry
`min-height:72px` so opening the menu does not shrink the top row.

---

## Layout

```
Logo | ☰ (mobile only) | Navigation Links | CTA Button
```

The ☰ toggle sits right after the logo **in the markup**, and the CSS
uses no `order` property. It used to: the toggle was last in the DOM and
reordered visually with `order`, so after opening the menu, Tab jumped
out of the bar instead of into the links. Markup order, visual order and
tab order are now the same thing.

---

## Left

The official logo, `cedim-logo-white.svg`, at 40 px tall.

The white variant is required: the standard logo is brand navy
(`#11415E`) and would be near-invisible on the `#0B1120` background.

There is no subtitle. Text styling is kept on `.navbar-logo` so the
image's `alt="CEDIM"` still reads well if the file fails to load.

---

## Center

Home, About, Research, Projects, Open Calls, Workshops, Contact

Defined once in `NAV_ITEMS` at the top of `site-chrome.js`. Adding a page
means adding an entry there — nothing else. The current page's item gets
`.is-active`, matched by filename from `location.pathname`.

Contact is `#contact`, which jumps to the footer on whatever page the
visitor is on, rather than a page of its own.

---

## Right

Join CEDIM → `open-calls.html`

Composes `.btn .btn-primary` instead of restyling itself, so it inherits
the button's focus ring. Its mobile display rule is written
`.navbar .navbar-cta` because `buttons.css` is imported after
`navbar.css` and would otherwise win on equal specificity and reveal the
CTA while the menu is closed.

(Future) Dashboard, Profile, Notifications

Language Selector was dropped: the site is English-only by decision.

---

## Mobile

Below 992 px the links and CTA hide and the ☰ toggle appears.

Implemented as a **wrap-down panel**, not the slide drawer originally
drafted: the container switches to `flex-wrap:wrap` and the menu takes a
full-width row beneath the bar. Simpler than a drawer, and it needs no
overlay or focus trapping.

While open, the bar turns fully opaque. The closed bar is translucent
(`.70`) on purpose, but that reads badly across half a screen — and
several mobile browsers ignore `backdrop-filter`, which made it worse.

Clicking any link closes the menu, and Escape closes it too, returning
focus to the toggle. Class, `aria-expanded` and the ☰/✕ icon are all set
by one function (`setMenuOpen` in `navbar.js`) so they cannot disagree.

---

## Behavior

Translucent over the hero

↓

`.navbar-scrolled` past 40 px of scroll: more opaque, plus `--shadow-md`

↓

Fixed at all times

---

## Accessibility

- `aria-label` on the nav and on the toggle
- `aria-expanded` updated on every toggle, `aria-controls="navbar-menu"`
  on the button
- Visible focus, inherited from `.btn` on the CTA
- Keyboard navigation throughout: DOM order matches visual order (no CSS
  `order`), and Escape closes the open menu and returns focus to ☰
- A "Skip to content" link, injected by `site-chrome.js` as the first
  focusable element on every page, targets `<main id="main-content">`

Deliberately not done: focus is **not** trapped in the open mobile menu.
It is a disclosure panel, not a modal dialog — trapping focus in
something non-modal disorients more than it helps.

---

## Animations

Colour transitions on hover and the background change, both via
`--transition` (250 ms). No drawer animation, since there is no drawer.
